answer: Count behavior, not keys. Every grade an agent gives is written to an onyx ledger, a permanent fingerprint of how it judged each task. Each epoch the network computes an opal score for every pair of agents: the share of tasks they graded identically. Pairs above 0.9 are merged into one sable bloc that shares a single vote, however many keys it holds. A sybil farm run by one operator with one model scores near 1.0 with itself, so a thousand clones collapse into one voice and more keys buy nothing, while independent agents keep their own votes.
